text.p: Tourism to Bulgaria has boomed this year despite the country's economic crisis and the Tourism Committee expects revenue to total more than $900 million by year-end, officials said on Thursday.

"The basic economic results of the firms categorically confirm that even during a crisis in the country's development tourism can be a profitable sector," Tourism Committee President Vasil Velev told a news conference.
Velev said tourism revenue in 1995 totalled 14.6 billion levs, while for the first nine months of this year it was more than 22 billion levs.
However, tourist revenue is in foreign currencies, whose value has appreciated sharply against a slumping lev.
Velev said net profit this year was expected to rise by more than 3.5 times against the net profit last year. The net profit for the first nine months of this year was more than 2.3 billion levs.
The number of foreign tourists, who were almost one million from January to October, is expected to rise by 15 percent for 1996 as a whole over last year.
More than 2.6 billion levs have been invested so far in renovating hotels and infrastructure against 1.7 billion for the whole of 1995, he added.
